I have farmed this land since I was a young woman. My plot is about 3 mu. I do not read books or government pamphlets. I watch what my neighbors plant and I remember what my mother and husband taught me. I do what I know.

Every year I plant wheat in October after the summer corn comes off. Then when the wheat is harvested in June, I plant corn right away on the same ground. I have done this my whole life. There is no reason to change. My son borrows the tractor from the village contractor to plow and plant for me — I cannot do that heavy work anymore.

For seeds, I buy whatever the cooperative store in town sells. They have the better seeds now, the ones that yield more. I do not save my own seed anymore like I did when I was young — those old varieties gave less. For fertilizer, I ask my neighbor Wang's son what he uses and I do the same. We put down the compound fertilizer when planting and then spread some urea when the wheat is tall. For corn I do the same. I use a bit more than they say because I want to make sure it grows well — I cannot afford a bad harvest.

Water — I pump from the well three times for wheat: once before the ground freezes, once when it joints, once when it heads. For corn I usually water once if the summer rains are late.

For pests I spray twice on wheat — once for weeds after it comes up in autumn, once in spring for aphids and rust. For corn just once for the army worm if it comes.
